data.body:
## The stale global rebar was not normal -- the hourly updater has been dead for 119 runs

The user asked whether this environment has an auto-update keeping rebar in sync with origin/main.
It does, and it is BROKEN. I had treated the 195-commits-behind global build as an ambient fact and
merely routed around it; it is actually a five-day outage of the update mechanism, affecting every
session on this host.

Filed ae97-a37b-9fa3-413a / princely-courageous-milksnake, priority 1.

ROOT CAUSE -- an inverted assumption, not a missing upgrade.
rebar-dev-update.sh:18 hardcodes UV_BIN=${REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/bin/uv}, and :120 orders
PATH to keep Homebrew authoritative with the stated reason at :116-118: 'Keep Homebrew before
~/.local/bin so the obsolete standalone uv there cannot shadow the pinned UV_BIN.' Measured today:
/opt/homebrew/bin/uv is 0.12.6 (2026-08-25); /Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/uv is 0.12.7 (2026-08-27).
The premise inverted -- Homebrew is now the stale side -- so the guard written to prevent selecting
a stale uv is the mechanism selecting one. pyproject.toml:346 pins required-version = '==0.12.7',
uv reads it itself and fails fast, so every hourly 'uv sync' aborts. 118 of 119 rejections are this;
one is a transient fetch-pack early EOF at the checkout stage.

SAME PIN, THIRD CONSUMER. required-version '==0.12.7' (commit 7501cc1d602d) is the same pin whose
floating uv:latest Dockerfile tags caused the multi-hour MCP outage under bug febd. That fix pinned
the three infra/compose Dockerfiles and extended scripts/check_uv_pin.py to scan them. This host's
updater is a third consumer that was never brought along -- and it is out of check_uv_pin.py's reach
because it is a machine-local, git-ignored script. Linked relates_to febd.

THE DETECTION GAP IS THE WORSE HALF. docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md documents a
REJECT_STREAK_ALERT (default 3) added after 'the b477339a99 incident: 43 hourly sync rejections,
~48 commits behind, no signal'. That alert is firing correctly every hour and failing to deliver
every time: AuthorizationError, IAM user in account 820258254566 publishing to an SNS topic in
account 896586841071, no resource-based policy permitting it. Streak 119 against a threshold of 3,
zero operator signal -- a strictly worse recurrence of the exact incident the alert exists to
prevent. So AC4 requires a LOCAL detector that does not depend on the remote sink at all.

IMPACT WORTH BEING BLUNT ABOUT: any plan-review or completion-verifier verdict produced through the
global rebar on this host in the last five days used a build whose own advisory says results 'can
be wrong in ways the verdict cannot show'. That is not limited to this session.

Secondary: launchd.err.log shows the pruner failing with 'Directory not empty' on release dirs, and
releases/5fb693345b0c...1559 is a 3-entry stub from a partially built release. At ~346 MB per
release dir this is disk-ceiling relevant, so linked relates_to epic 6202.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER FRAMING: I told a subagent to use the worktree venv 'because the global
build is stale'. That was the right instruction for the wrong reason -- I presented a broken
updater as a standing environmental condition. The venv-on-PATH rule remains correct regardless,
but the staleness itself is a bug with a ticket, not a fact of the environment.
